title: Custody death inquest ordered
article: The family of Clayton Willey is getting their wish. A coroner's inquest into the death of 32-year-old Clayton Alvin Willey will be conducted, commencing October 18 of this year.

Presiding Coroner David Coverdale, along with a five-person jury will hear evidence from witnesses and review evidence collected in the case of the man some say died as a result of brute police force.
The police maintain they did only what was necessary in the subduing of a suspect; the death was unfortunate, unintentional and outside their control.
The family and supporters of Willey have been calling for an independent audit of the events leading to his death ever since.
The inquest will take place at 1011 Fourth Avenue, in the Aleza Room. It is anticipated to take seven to 10 days to complete.
